_comment: Incident Response Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; pairs naturally with the AU plan since incidents are detected via the audit pipeline. Note the meta-quirk: IR-8 (Incident Response Plan) is satisfied BY this very document, so the §5.8 implementation block typically references the document itself.
title: Incident Response Plan
description: Documents how the organization prepares for, detects, contains, eradicates, recovers from, and learns from cybersecurity incidents affecting the system. Covers the controls of the IR family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-61 r2 (Computer Security Incident Handling Guide).
intro_template:
This Incident Response Plan documents the incident-response approach for {system_name}. It establishes the roles, processes, communication paths, and timelines used to handle cybersecurity incidents from initial detection through post-incident lessons learned.

The scope covers preparation (training, exercises, tooling), detection and analysis, containment / eradication / recovery, post-incident activity, external reporting, and information-spillage response within the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (Incident Response family), NIST SP 800-61 r2 (Computer Security Incident Handling Guide), and the CISA Federal Government Cybersecurity Incident & Vulnerability Response Playbooks.

This document satisfies the IR-8 control requirement for the system to maintain a documented incident-response plan.
approach_template: Cybersecurity incidents affecting {system_name} are handled by {irt_name}, using {ticketing_tool} as the case-management system of record. Detection draws on {detection_sources} and decision-making is informed by {threat_intel_sources}. Response follows the four phases of NIST SP 800-61 r2: Preparation; Detection and Analysis; Containment, Eradication, and Recovery; and Post-Incident Activity. Severity-tier classification, containment SLAs, external reporting timelines, and the information-spillage process are documented in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Incident-response performance for {system_name} is tracked continuously via the metrics in §6.1 (mean time to detect, mean time to contain, false-positive rate, exercise findings closed). Threat-intelligence feeds are reviewed for newly relevant indicators on the cadence in §6.2. Lessons learned from each incident drive plan revisions; the document is reviewed at the cadence below regardless of incident occurrence.
integration_template: This Incident Response Plan does not stand alone. The AU family supplies the audit records and detection signals that initiate incident response; the SI family provides the system-monitoring infrastructure and integrity tooling that surface candidate incidents; CP coordination ensures recovery actions align with continuity-of-operations objectives. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where IR-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

commonly_inheritable_controls.from: Enterprise security-awareness and IR training program
Enterprise SOC / CSIRT and external IR retainer

family_questions.label: Approach basics
family_questions.description: IRT structure, ticketing platform, and the primary detection sources that feed the team.

questions.label: Incident response team (IRT) name and structure
questions.help: What the team is called and how it's structured (e.g., '24/7 SOC + on-call IRT', 'Enterprise CSIRT', 'Combined SOC/IRT under the CISO').

questions.label: Case-management / ticketing system of record
questions.help: Tool that holds incident cases (e.g., ServiceNow Security Operations, Jira Service Management, TheHive, Demisto / Cortex XSOAR, IBM Resilient).

questions.label: Primary detection source summary (one-line for §4 narrative)
questions.help: Brief phrase summarizing what generates incident candidates. Detail goes in the dedicated sub-section.

questions.label: Threat-intelligence sources summary
questions.help: Brief phrase (e.g., 'CISA AIS, MS-ISAC, vendor threat feeds, internal honeypot data').

family_questions.label: Incident Classification & Severity
family_questions.description: How incidents are categorized and prioritized; containment SLAs by tier.

questions.label: Severity tiers used
options: High / Tier 2 (single-system compromise or data exposure)

questions.label: Containment SLA per tier
questions.help: Target time from detection to containment, by severity tier (e.g., 'Critical: 1h, High: 4h, Medium: 24h, Low: best-effort within 5 business days').

questions.label: Escalation thresholds
questions.help: When does an incident escalate to executive leadership / AO / external IR retainer? Define triggers (severity, scope, time elapsed).

family_questions.label: Detection Sources
family_questions.description: What feeds candidate incidents into the queue.

questions.label: Detection sources used
options: Cloud provider alerts (GuardDuty, Defender for Cloud)

questions.label: Alert routing into the case queue
questions.help: How alerts from each source land in the case-management system. Auto-promotion rules, deduplication, severity scoring.

questions.label: False-positive handling
questions.help: How recurring false positives are tuned out without losing visibility into real signals. Exception-rule register and review cadence.

questions.label: User incident-reporting channel
questions.help: How users report suspected incidents (e.g., 'phishing@org email auto-feeds the queue; ServiceNow Security Incident form').

family_questions.label: Handling Phases (NIST SP 800-61 r2)
family_questions.description: Preparation; Detection & Analysis; Containment, Eradication, Recovery; Post-Incident.

questions.label: Preparation activities
questions.help: What's prepared in advance: jump-kit contents, known-good images, contact rosters, evidence-collection tooling.

questions.label: Analysis workflow
questions.help: How an alert becomes an incident: triage steps, scoping, attribution, classification. Reference SOAR playbooks if used.

questions.label: Containment strategy
questions.help: Standard containment options (network isolation, account disable, host quarantine). Approval thresholds for containment that disrupts operations.

questions.label: Eradication and recovery
questions.help: How threats are removed and systems restored. References CM-2 baseline restoration and CP backup-restore procedures.

questions.label: Post-incident review process
questions.help: Lessons-learned cadence (within N days of resolution), participation, and how findings drive plan revisions and POA&M items.

family_questions.label: External Reporting & Notifications
family_questions.description: Who outside the organization must be notified, and on what timeline.

questions.label: Reporting timelines
questions.help: Mandatory timelines per recipient (e.g., 'CISA major incident: within 1 hour of declaration; PII breach: 72h GDPR / state-specific'). CISA reference: Federal Incident Notification Guidelines.

questions.label: Default Traffic Light Protocol marking
questions.help: Default sensitivity marking on outbound IR communications. Most internal-IR comms start TLP:AMBER+STRICT.

questions.label: External-communications owner
questions.help: Role responsible for external messaging (typically Public Affairs / Comms in coordination with Legal and the IRT).

family_questions.label: Training and Exercises
family_questions.description: Role-based training cadence and exercise programs (IR-2, IR-3).

questions.label: IR-specific training cadence
options: Quarterly for IRT + annual refresh for general staff

questions.label: Exercise cadence
options: Monthly tabletops + quarterly functional + annual full-scale

questions.label: After-action / lessons-learned process
questions.help: How findings from exercises and real incidents are tracked to closure (POA&M? Internal tracker?). Cadence for re-validating closure.

family_questions.label: Information Spillage Response (IR-9)
family_questions.description: Process for handling unauthorized disclosure of classified or controlled information.

questions.label: What constitutes spillage in this system
questions.help: Categories of information whose disclosure triggers spillage response (CUI / FOUO / classified / PII / PHI / etc.) and the threshold for declaration.

questions.label: Spillage response steps
questions.help: Steps when spillage is suspected or confirmed: containment (isolate affected systems), notification chain, scope assessment, sanitization plan, retention of evidence.

questions.label: Sanitization approach
questions.help: How affected systems / storage are sanitized per NIST SP 800-88 r1. Reference MP-6 if applicable.

questions.label: Spillage response lead role
questions.help: Role responsible for coordinating spillage response (often the ISSO + Privacy Officer for PII).

family_questions.label: IRT Scope and Membership
family_questions.description: Who's on the team and how they're contacted.

questions.label: Approximate IRT size
questions.help: Order of magnitude (e.g., '~10 analysts across 3 tiers').

questions.label: Area of responsibility (AOR)
questions.help: What systems and populations the team covers (single system vs enterprise).

questions.label: Primary IRT contact method
questions.help: How users / on-call engineers reach the IRT (e.g., 'PagerDuty service ir-soc; phishing@org for low-priority reports').

questions.label: External IR retainer (if any)
questions.help: Third-party IR firm on retainer for surge support (e.g., Mandiant, CrowdStrike Services, Unit 42).

family_questions.label: Incident Response Metrics & KPIs
family_questions.description: Metrics tracked to demonstrate IR control effectiveness over time.

questions.label: Tracked metrics
suggestions: False-positive rate (% of alerts triaged out as FP)
Number of incidents per quarter (by severity)

family_questions.label: Threat Intelligence Consumption
family_questions.description: Sources, ingestion, and IOC sweeping cadence.

questions.label: Threat-intel feeds subscribed
options: Commercial feed (Mandiant / Recorded Future / CrowdStrike / etc.)
Vendor product feeds (built into EDR / SIEM)

questions.label: IOC ingestion mechanism
questions.help: How indicators flow from feeds into detection (TIP, MISP, direct SIEM watchlist, EDR threat-feed import).

questions.label: Retroactive IOC sweep cadence
questions.help: How often historical logs are searched for newly-published indicators (e.g., 'Daily for high-priority feeds; weekly comprehensive sweep').

family_questions.label: Cross-references to other RMF artifacts
family_questions.description: Where this plan plugs into the broader RMF package.

questions.label: SSP section reference
questions.help: Where in the SSP the IR control implementations are summarized (e.g., 'SSP §13.6').

questions.label: POA&M ID prefix for IR findings
questions.help: Convention for IR-related POA&M items (e.g., 'POAM-IR-').

questions.label: AU plan cross-reference
questions.help: How audit records and SIEM detections from the AU plan feed incident detection. SIEM index, log sources, retention.

questions.label: SI plan cross-reference
questions.help: How system-monitoring (SI-4), malware protection (SI-3), and integrity verification (SI-7) generate IR signals.

questions.label: CP plan cross-reference
questions.help: How recovery from incidents coordinates with the contingency plan's restoration procedures.

questions.label: CA-7 continuous-monitoring strategy reference
questions.help: Pointer to the CA-7 monitoring strategy document tying IR continuous-monitoring metrics to the broader ConMon plan.

glossary.definition: Any observable occurrence in an information system or network that has a negative consequence — e.g., a system crash. Not all adverse events become incidents.
Document produced after an exercise or real incident summarizing what happened, what worked, what didn't, and corrective actions.
Chronological documentation of who handled a piece of evidence, when, and what was done with it. Required for evidence to be admissible.
Phase of incident response that limits damage and prevents spread, before full eradication is possible.
Computer Security Incident Response Team — a formalized IRT, often with regional or sector responsibility.
Phase of incident response during which an event is identified as a candidate incident.
Phase of incident response that removes the threat from the environment (delete malware, close attacker accounts, patch the exploited vulnerability).
Any observable occurrence in a system or network. Most events are benign; a small subset are adverse events; a smaller subset are incidents.
An alert or finding that, on investigation, was not actually a security incident. Tuning false positives down without losing true-positive sensitivity is a continuous calibration.
A live drill in which IR processes are exercised against a simulated incident, often using technical tooling but without affecting production.
An adverse event that has been determined to have a security impact (compromise, policy violation, etc.) and triggers the IR process.
The person leading response to a specific incident, holding decision authority over containment and recovery actions.
The team responsible for handling cybersecurity incidents. May be combined with the SOC, may be a separate escalation tier, may be augmented by an external retainer.
A behavioral pattern indicating an attack technique is being attempted (e.g., process-injection sequences). Compares to IOC, which is artifact-based.
An artifact that indicates a system has been compromised — file hash, IP address, domain, registry key, etc.
Unauthorized disclosure of classified or controlled information to a system not authorized to handle it. Triggers IR-9 response.
Insights captured during post-incident review — what worked, what failed, what to do differently. Drives plan revision and training updates.
A globally accessible knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques. Frequently used for IR analysis and reporting structure.
A documented sequence of steps for handling a specific category of incident, often automated in a SOAR platform.
Structured review (NIST SP 800-61 r2 phase 4) where the IRT and stakeholders examine what happened and capture lessons learned.
Phase of incident response that restores affected systems to operational state, often using CM-2 baseline restoration and CP backup procedures.
Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response — a class of tools that automate IR playbooks and integrate with SIEM, ticketing, and security tools.
A discussion-based drill in which IR participants walk through a hypothetical scenario without touching production systems.
Information about adversaries — their tactics, techniques, infrastructure, and indicators — that informs detection and response.
A set of designations used to ensure that sensitive information is shared with the appropriate audience. Levels: TLP:RED (named recipients only), AMBER, GREEN, CLEAR.
Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures — the way an adversary operates, useful for detection and attribution.
